Usage¶

This page explains the command line arguments TIARS designer takes to run and a usage example.

Inputs¶

Once TIARS-Designer is installed, the following arguments are required to run the tool.

Required Inputs¶

Argument

Description

endogenous_seq

The full endogenous sequence to be edited. Must extend at least 85 nucleotides upstream(5’) of the Cas protein cut and 50 nucleotides downstream (3’) of the Cas cut.

gRNA_start

The location in the sequence* of the beginning of the guide RNA (in this case the PAM site is considered to be part of the guide RNA)

gRNA_end

The location in the sequence* of the end of the guide RNA (again, PAM is considered part of the guideRNA). This should correspond to the location of the first bp after the last bp of the guide RNA, such that slicing the string in python (e.g. endogenous_seq[gRNA_start: gRNA_end]) would yield the full gRNA

PAM_start

The location in the sequence* of the beginning of the PAM site

which_PAM

specifies which type of PAM your experiment uses. Right now Cas9 (CCN and NGG) and Cpf1 (TVVV and BAAA) are supported. NOTE: put the generic sequence of the PAM rather than the exact one the sample uses (e.g. put NGG rather than AGG)

AA_change_site

The location in the sequence* of the codon that will contain desired CRISPR edit (even if the actual edit changes the second or third basepair in the codon, this value should still correspond to the first basepair in the codon)

new codon

The basepair sequence of the new codon containing the edit (for example, if you wanted to change a GGA glycine to an AGA arginine, you would put AGA)

sample_name

The name of the locus/sample, which will be used to name the output folder and files

–codon-usage-tsv

A tsv of codon usage frequency values for the organism used. The tsv should have one codon per line in the format: [codon]>[frequency] (e.g. ‘UGA>1.4’) where ‘>’ represents a tab. The default tsv is for zebrafish. Organism specific codon frequencies can be found at the Kazusa Codon usage Database

–single-enzyme-filters

A list of single enzyme filters to run. To run all of the single-enzyme filters (recommended), input ‘all’. The filters names that can be used are: - no_sandwiched_cutsites - no_endogenous_cutsites_within_Nnt_of_novel_cutsite - novel_site_depends_on_at_least_two_substitutions - num_recognition_sites_equals_num_cutsites - no_unneeded_substitutions . See Filters for a complete description of the Filters.

–enzyme-pair-filters

A list of enzyme pair filters to run. To run all of the enzyme-pair filters(recommended), input ‘all’. The filter names that can be used are: - at_least_one_has_endogenous_site - both_have_endogenous_sites - compatible_polarity - both_Renzymes_depend_on_at_least_one_unique_substitution . See Filters for a complete description of the Filters.

  • NOTE: any time the ‘location in the sequence’ of an element is mentioned, this is referring to it coordinate in the sequence, where the first basepair in the sequence is considered 0, the second basepair is 1, the third is 2, etc.

Optional Inputs¶

The tool has the option to provide a custom list of desired restriction enzymes to use and to output passing percentages for each filter.

Argument

Description

–min_Rsite_distance

The minimum allowable distance (in basepairs) between the novel restriction site and any endogenous restriction sites for a given enzyme. This is to avoid having fragment sizes that are too similar to be able to tell the difference between a novel site cut and and endogenous site cut. This is the value used in the ‘no Endogenous Cutsites within 5Nt of Novel Site’ filter (see :ref: Filters). Default=5

–enzymes

A tsv/txt file containing a list of restriction enzymes to use (must be in the Bio.Restriction database, case sensitive). The list should have one enzyme per line Default= Bio.Restriction ‘CommonOnly’ list of commonly used enzymes.

–verbose

If this flag is included, output tsv files with passing percentages for each filter as well as raw the total number of candidates before and after filtering.

Example Usage¶

The following example shows a sequence with its coordinates mapped out for easy viewing of the PAM_start, and gRNA start and end sites (in reality this sequence would have to be longer to go in the tool, it’s been shortened for easier display).

# coordinate 0         1         2         3         4         5
#            012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890

# sequence   GCTGGTGGCCCCCAAATATTCAGGTTTAATGTTCACTCTGCAACACTCTTT
#                       |                    | |
#               gRNA_start and       AA_change gRNA_end
#                  PAM_start

For this example, the codon to be changed is the TCA starting at coordinate 32, and we want to change it to TTA. The gRNA sequence is CCAAATATTCAGGTTTAATGTTC. This example would have the following values:

sample: example_sequence
AA_change_site: 32
new_codon: TTA
PAM_start: 11
gRNA_start: 11
gRNA_end: 34
which_PAM: CCN
sequence: GCTGGTGGCCCCCAAATATTCAGGTTTAATGTTCACTCTGCAACACTCTTT

An example command to run this sample would be:

tiarsdesigner                                                        \
GCTGGTGGCCCCCAAATATTCAGGTTTAATGTTCACTCTGCAACACTCTTT                  \ # Endogenous Sequence
11                                                                   \ # gRNA_start
34                                                                   \ # gRNA_end
11                                                                   \ # PAM_start
CCN                                                                  \ # Which_PAM
32                                                                   \ # AA_change_site
TTA                                                                  \ # new_codon
example_sequence                                                     \ # locus_name
--single-enzyme-filters all                                          \ # Run all single-enzyme filters
--enzyme-pair-filters no_unneeded_substitutions compatible_polarity  \ # only run two enzyme pair filters (to show usage)
--codon-usage-tsv /path/to/codon_usage.tsv                           \ # Codon usage file
--enzymes /path/to/enzymes.tsv                                       \ # Path to custom enzyme list
--verbose                                                            \ # Output filter stat tsvs
